iterations.theme: Analysis of the Hajduk - Dinamo derby at Poljud and problems in the play of the 'Blues'

sections.subtitle: Introduction and the English adventure: From visiting Jakirović to Old Trafford
sections.screenshot_description: Profa and Denis report from England with props and recount their visit to the Manchester United match
sections.content:
The episode begins with a report from England, where host Profa and interlocutor Denis found themselves on a sort of football adventure. As Denis explains, they took advantage of a unique opportunity and were guests of former Dinamo coach Sergej Jakirović. As part of the visit, they spent time at Hull City's training ahead of their match with Everton, while on the very day of the derby they visited Old Trafford in Manchester and the clash between Manchester United and Tottenham.

Although the overall ambiance of the English stadiums left a great impression on both of them, the entire mood was spoiled by the outcome of the derby at Poljud, which they watched from the hotel room immediately before leaving for the match. Profa joked with a reference to the well-known saying about how in difficult moments it is “better to cry in a Porsche”, suggesting that it is easier to endure Dinamo's defeat while being in the cradle of football. Nevertheless, Denis emphasizes that opening difficult topics and a summary of Dinamo's suffering on the pitch await them.

sections.subtitle: Poljud warning: Hajduk's deserved victory and Bamba's dominance
sections.screenshot_description: Denis gestures speaking about how Hajduk completely outplayed Dinamo's defense
sections.content:
Opening the analysis of the derby itself, Profa recalls the famous interview of Kobe Bryant who, after a defeat in the finals, did not want to look for a single alibi. Denis completely agreed with such an approach, clearly stating that Hajduk was better and celebrated completely deservedly. Although refereeing decisions and pitch conditions can be dissected, Denis underlines that the cause of Dinamo's stumble does not lie in them.

Denis believes that, in place of the club management, he would print Hajduk's lineup and a framed picture of their wing forward Bamba Sanyang and hang them in Dinamo's dressing room as a permanent reminder. According to his view, Bamba completely dominated Dinamo's defensive line, which he considers devastating given that Dinamo individually possesses at least ten better players in the starting eleven. Instead of imposing authority, Dinamo spent most of the match in a passive low or medium block, without recognizable dynamics and hunger for victory.

sections.subtitle: Tactical blunders and questionable forcing of not fully fit Luka Stojković
sections.screenshot_description: Profa asks a question about Kovačević's substitutions and bringing Stojković into the match
sections.content:
Commenting on coach Mario Kovačević's setup, Denis points out that the moves made around the 60th minute of the match were a direct admission of mistakes in match preparation. Kovačević practically nullified his own initial plan with a triple substitution. A special focus was placed on the introduction of Luka Stojković, about whom the coach himself stated that he had completed his first full training session only two days earlier.

Denis considers that there was no sporting or medical logic in introducing the not fully fit Stojković onto a waterlogged, heavy, and muddy Poljud pitch, risking his health in a match that was already devoid of real rhythm. Profa recalls that fans had already previously reproached the coach for forcing key recovering players in the Cup against Vukovar. Both conclude that Dinamo's performance at this moment does not inspire confidence ahead of the crucial European test against Anderlecht, where the team has an imperative to awaken from lethargy.

sections.subtitle: Worrying decline in Europe and lucky scraping through the season
sections.screenshot_description: Denis lists Dinamo's European matches in detail and warns of a downward trend
sections.content:
The discussion then expanded to the broader context of Dinamo's performances this season. Although the coaching staff can cite that the club's goal was qualification for the Europa League, Denis and Profa emphasize that with last season's European coefficient the club had an open path toward the Champions League, but the trend of performances is evidently downward.

Denis recalls the fact that against Swiss Thun Dinamo advanced with a great deal of luck and the help of an opponent player's sending-off, where in neither match was it more dominant. A similar thing happened against Viking and Hapoel Beer Sheva, with the latter match being marked as one of the luckiest victories in Kovačević's tenure despite a devastating idea of play. Profa adds that the three-month impression was softened by the international break, but the statistics of only three victories in nine more serious clashes clearly show the scale of the crisis in play.

sections.subtitle: Criticism of the summer transfer window: Squad management and Boban's responsibility
sections.screenshot_description: Denis talks about bad moves in the transfer window and the atmosphere within the club
sections.content:
Denis voiced fierce criticism regarding the club's transfer policy, calling out Zvonimir Boban and the management for a very poorly executed transfer window in vital positions. In his judgment, a person of such football authority and resources should not have allowed himself the bringing of unready players and lapses in key spots in the team, including the goalkeeper question.

The paradox in the back line was especially highlighted, where Niko Galešić, despite proven reliability, warms the bench while Sergi Dominguez receives limitless trust despite frequent blunders. Also, Denis looked back at the light dismissal of young domestic players like Fran Topić and the status of Lukas Kačavenda. He warns that negative tensions around the stadium and club bodies spilled over into the dressing room, whereby coach Kovačević lost the earlier firm shield that enabled him unhindered management of the team.

sections.subtitle: Dissecting the goals at Poljud and painful dependence on Josip Mišić
sections.screenshot_description: Profa analyzes the set piece on Hajduk's first goal and the lack of creation in the midfield
sections.content:
Analyzing the leading goal of the Split team, Denis points out a tactical detail in which a Hajduk player set a precise block on a Dinamo defender during a set piece, which enabled the passage of the ball after an excellent cross by Šimun Hrgović. Scott McKenna did not see the ball at all in the process, which is why Denis considers him merely a victim of an unfortunate set of circumstances, and not the main culprit.

However, the fundamental problem of the 'Blues' once again manifested itself in the organization of play without Josip Mišić. Denis warns that it is unacceptable for Dinamo to appear completely powerless as soon as it lacks its main midfielder. Instead of the formation and mechanisms adapting to his absence, Dinamo stubbornly attempted to play according to old templates, which boiled down to sterile hoofing of long balls forward by the center-backs. The attempt for other players to merely act like Mišić turned out to be a complete failure.

sections.subtitle: The question of right back: Pierre-Gabriel and center-back illogicalities
sections.screenshot_description: Denis explains why he believes Pierre-Gabriel does not meet the criteria for Dinamo
sections.content:
A large part of the discussion was dedicated to the right back position and the performance of Ronaël Pierre-Gabriel. Denis openly questions his quality for Dinamo's high ambitions, emphasizing that a player of those years has no resale value and that an occasional good cross cannot mask modest tactical and defensive capabilities. The question of the purpose of Dinamo's youth academy arises if the club must force mediocre foreign solutions in that position.

Additional revolt is caused by the fact that Niko Galešić has already successfully fulfilled the role of right back several times and stabilized the defensive phase, yet remained outside the starting lineup. Denis attributes such a move either to the imposition of solutions from club offices or to Kovačević's tactical disorientation. Also, center-back Sergi Dominguez, who once again played an insecure derby with a series of mistakes, still enjoys enormous credit which, in Denis's judgment, he does not justify with performances on the pitch.

sections.subtitle: Hajduk's energy and aggressiveness: Won duels and dominance on the pitch
sections.screenshot_description: Profa reads viewers' comments about Hajduk's approach and hunger for victory
sections.content:
Commenting on a message from viewer Ana Lovrić, who noticed that Hajduk, after a series of years, did not retreat into a low block against Dinamo, the interlocutors admitted that the Split team deserved all praise for a brave approach. Denis and Profa emphasize that Hajduk imposed itself through energy, physical strength, and uncompromising winning of the so-called “second balls”. In the middle of the pitch, the home players were regularly first to the ball and more aggressive in every contact.

Bamba was constantly breaking through on the wing and creating havoc, which Denis underlines as the key contrast compared to the anemic Dinamo. Although Denis notes that Bamba is not a technically refined player, his speed, explosiveness, and hunger for duels were an unsolvable riddle for the defense of the 'Blues'. For Dinamo, it is a devastating fact that the opponent looked hungrier and more compact, despite the fact that Dinamo's squad on paper has significantly higher earnings and individual reputation.

sections.subtitle: Fiasco of wing forwards and questioning the 4-3-3 system
sections.screenshot_description: Denis shows with his hands the movements of the wingers and explains the tactical deficiencies of the formation
sections.content:
Profa and Denis dissected in detail Kovačević's forcing of the 4-3-3 system. Profa ironically observes that this formation in theory serves to maximize the use of wings, while Dinamo's wingers at Poljud were completely invisible and tactically disoriented. Denis rejects modern analytical platitudes about how wing forwards cannot play on opposite flanks, emphasizing that a player of that level must possess basic tactical literacy and hold the corridor instead of constantly fleeing into the crowd in the middle.

They also touched upon the significant drop in form of the midfielders compared to last season, with Dion Drena Beljo receiving the only passing grade in the attack. Denis praises Beljo's work ethic and continuous finishing despite the fact that on the day of the derby he also had health issues. Still, Denis wonders whether it makes any sense at all for Dinamo to stubbornly copy Barcelona's 4-3-3 system when it does not have the player profile for such dominance, instead of developing flexibility and pragmatism for derbies and European clashes.

sections.subtitle: Poljud mud and Kovačević's coaching cycle: Is the story coming to an end?
sections.screenshot_description: Denis draws a parallel with marriage while speaking about the relationship between Kovačević and Dinamo's dressing room
sections.content:
Reflecting on the bad weather in Split, Denis with a dose of humor rejects the rain as an alibi for the 'Blues', recalling that Dinamo was most dangerous only at moments when the pitch turned into “water polo”, while Hajduk dominated under more regular conditions. The central discussion then focused on Kovačević's status. Denis uses a vivid comparison to a marriage of two good people between whom the energy was lost — the fact that cooperation no longer functions does not mean that Kovačević is a bad coach, but that the cycle has reached its natural saturation, just as happened to Jürgen Klopp or Pep Guardiola.

Denis recalls that Kovačević fulfilled all set goals last season, but notes that at Dinamo he actually never received completely free hands for creation and changes of system such as he successfully implemented at Slaven Belupo. The impression is that the team cries out for shock therapy and that the encounter against Anderlecht could be the last opportunity for a turnaround before inevitable cuts on the bench.

sections.subtitle: Officiating of Igor Pajač: Circus with cards without seeking alibis
sections.screenshot_description: Profa and Denis discuss referee Igor Pajač's criteria and fouls for a red card
sections.content:
In the final part of the derby analysis, the officiating of Igor Pajač also came up. Denis emphasizes that Pajač was not the cause of Dinamo's defeat, but sharply criticizes his style of managing the match. The referee failed to show early yellow cards for heavy fouls and unsporting reactions, whereby he lost control, only to then resolve every contentious situation with long conversations and explanations with the players instead of a clear application of the rules.

Both agree that the tackle on Dinamo's footballer on the muddy pitch was on the verge of a straight red card, which Profa initially interpreted as a potential scenario from Thun where the team could have gotten away undeservedly. Still, Denis refuses for the blame to be shifted onto the referee because there are ten objective playing reasons for the defeat. In the end, Profa ironically recalled the statistics of Pajač's derbies, in which Hajduk regularly achieves victories or draws, concluding that the 'Blues' must look for the causes of failure exclusively in their own play.

iterations.theme: English impressions, live viewers' questions, and the perspective of the championship continuation

sections.subtitle: English anecdotes: Cristiano Ronaldo scarf, National Football Museum, and Old Trafford
sections.screenshot_description: Profa shows souvenirs and talks about the visit to Old Trafford and the National Football Museum
sections.content:
After the analysis of the eternal derby at Poljud, the interlocutors looked back at their stay in England and football memories they gathered during the trip. Denis teased Profa because of the souvenirs he bought, pointing out scarves with the image of Cristiano Ronaldo that Profa wore around his neck.

Profa recounted the visit to the National Football Museum in Manchester, where he was intrigued by the representation of Cristiano Ronaldo, but the real experience followed with the arrival at Old Trafford. After they arrived by taxi in front of the iconic stadium immediately after watching Dinamo's defeat, the first image he caught sight of was that of Ronaldo's famous free kick against Portsmouth, where Niko Kranjčar was in the wall. Although huge demand reigned in the club shop and many items dedicated to the Portuguese ace were sold out, Profa managed to find the desired merchandise, which served as a perfect introduction into the more casual part of the show.

sections.subtitle: Viewers' questions: Main causes of Dinamo's decline, mental pressure, and bad transfer window
sections.screenshot_description: Denis and Profa discuss live viewers' questions about the reasons for the drop in Dinamo's form
sections.content:
By involving viewers in the live broadcast, a discussion was opened on the key reasons why Dinamo this season delivers significantly weaker performances compared to the previous one. To a question from one of the followers about the causes of the crisis, Profa highlighted the team's saturation with the coach and the psychological burden that accumulated after difficult matches and European stumbles, especially pointing out the shocking defeat against Viking from which the team and fans have not yet fully recovered.

Denis followed up by emphasizing how negative energy from the top of the club spilled over into the dressing room and coaching staff. He especially criticized the summer transfer window, labeling it one of the poorer in recent history, because the club did not adequately fill critical positions nor bring the player edge that was urgently needed for the parallel fight in Europe and the domestic championship. Although individual positive flashes from players coming off the bench were recorded, the general impression remains that the team seems deflated and without clear authoritative leadership.

sections.subtitle: Foreign or domestic referees: Disputes over officiating and refereeing organization in the HNL
sections.screenshot_description: Denis gestures energetically speaking against the introduction of foreign referees in the HNL
sections.content:
One of the more intriguing questions from viewers concerned bringing foreign referees for SuperSport HNL derbies. Denis stated an exceptionally firm and unwavering stance, asserting that he would ban the engagement of foreign referees by HNS decree. He believes that Croatia is not an uncivilized football environment like Greece or Turkey that cannot create conditions for a regular competition, and that constant appointment of foreigners is disastrous for the development and affirmation of domestic referees on the European stage.

Profa somewhat offered a more pragmatic view, considering that foreign referees would at least temporarily silence the eternal conspiracy theories and tensions that regularly accompany the derbies of Hajduk and Dinamo. Nevertheless, Denis remained with the stance that domestic referees must profile themselves in the biggest matches and that focusing on referee decisions after a derby is merely running away from real tactical and playing problems on the pitch.

sections.subtitle: Away record and fan bickering: Dinamo's black streak away from Maksimir
sections.screenshot_description: Profa and Denis analyze Dinamo's away match statistics
sections.content:
During the show, a statistical discussion opened about Dinamo's away record this season. Denis and Profa established a startling piece of data through conversation: in the current season outside its own stadium, Dinamo achieved only a minimal number of victories, singling out only a Cup match and the European clash against Žalgiris, while on away trips in Pula, Osijek, Split, and European clashes stumbles or draws against nominally considerably more modest opponents were regularly recorded.

This statistic also served as an occasion to comment on fan teasing in the broadcast chat, where Hajduk fans chimed in celebrating triumph and announcing the winning of the title. Denis joked at the expense of Profa's nervousness due to comments from the Split fans, while Profa countered with a reminder of Hajduk's multi-year drought in mutual derbies at Maksimir, concluding that the Split euphoria is premature despite Dinamo's current problems.

sections.subtitle: Anderlecht as a turning point for the coach and memories of the first steps in Dinamo's academy
sections.screenshot_description: Denis speaks about coach Vlado Novak and training in Dinamo's youth categories
sections.content:
Commenting on the immediate future of the Dinamo bench, Denis and Profa agreed that the upcoming Europa League match against Anderlecht should serve as a definitive and final test for the coach. Although Denis considers that the energy in the team is already irreversibly spent, Profa emphasized that an abrupt sacking before such an important European match does not guarantee a positive shock effect and that it is most proper to wait for the outcome of that clash before the board's final cuts.

Prompted by a viewer's question about their own football past, Denis nostalgically recalled his first football steps in Dinamo's open school. He described how as a six-year-old he saw an advertisement in Večernji list that his grandmother was reading, after which he applied for the selection of the 1991 generation. He highlighted coach Vlado Novak as a great pedagogue and expert in working with children, recalling how Andrej Kramarić achieved the greatest career from that generation, and he also mentioned coach Davor Blašković.

sections.subtitle: Impressions of England: Prices, Premier League tickets, and announcement of the match between Hull and Everton
sections.screenshot_description: The interlocutors compare living costs in England and comment on attending the match
sections.content:
In the continuation of the show, Denis and Profa shared general impressions of their stay in England, commenting on high costs and specificities of everyday life on the Island. Denis joked at the expense of English cuisine and breakfast with beans and noticed a noticeable number of homeless people on the streets, while Profa praised the traditional brick architecture and the relaxed nature of the local population despite the famous gloomy weather.

They also reflected on ticket prices for Premier League matches. Profa was pleasantly surprised by the fact that he managed to acquire a ticket for the derby of Manchester United and Tottenham for 80 pounds through official club membership, which he considers relatively affordable given the reputation of the clubs and the fact that it is Old Trafford. They also announced attending tomorrow's match between Hull City and Everton, where they are visiting former coach Sergej Jakirović.

sections.subtitle: Final conclusion: Pressure shifts onto Hajduk and a comment on Jakirović's public statement
sections.screenshot_description: Profa concludes the show and comments on media writings about Sergej Jakirović
sections.content:
Right before the end of the broadcast, Denis offered a summarizing conclusion about the state in the championship, asserting that after this derby all the pressure has shifted onto Hajduk's back. According to his words, the Split team now has a historic opportunity and losing the title to this kind of crisis-hit Dinamo would be tantamount to a complete debacle for them.

In the final minutes, Profa also reflected on media echoes of Sergej Jakirović's press conference in England. He expressed displeasure with the way certain domestic sports journalists reported the questions from that conference, suggesting sensationalism where there is none. They brought the show to an end with a message to the fans to follow further analyses, announcing new reports from the English tour and an analysis of the Hull City match.
